lead.headline: YS SHARMILA STOPPED FROM ENTERING YELAHANKA FAMILY HOME
lead.deck: Police cited an interim court order when the Andhra Pradesh Congress chief and her mother tried to reach the Bengaluru residence amid a dispute with her brother, Y S Jagan Mohan Reddy.
paragraphs: YS Sharmila and her mother, Y S Vijayalakshmi, were stopped by Bengaluru police on Sunday evening while trying to visit Yelahanka Palace, where the family of Sharmila’s brother, former Andhra Pradesh chief minister Y S Jagan Mohan Reddy, is staying.

Police cited an interim court order restraining Sharmila and her representatives from entering or interfering with the disputed property. Sharmila said she was unaware of the order and questioned why she was prevented from visiting what she considers a family home. The dispute has sharpened ahead of her daughter’s wedding later this week.

sidebarStory.headline: COP31 ENDS WITHOUT AN OVERARCHING CLIMATE DEAL
sidebarStory.subhead: Negotiators failed to agree after divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance.
paragraphs: The UN climate talks in Antalya ended without a consensus agreement after the final proposal omitted an explicit reference to fossil fuels. The European Union and several other countries rejected the text.
The negotiations ran almost 48 hours beyond their scheduled close. Developing countries also criticised the proposed climate-finance increase for lacking a clear baseline.

stories.headline: BMTC AUDIT FLAGS MORE THAN INR 4 CRORE IN ALLEGED IRREGULARITIES
paragraphs: An internal audit at BMTC’s Central Store-1 found alleged irregularities involving missing bus spare parts over five years. Wilson Garden police have registered an FIR naming 21 serving and retired officials and a private supplier.
The complaint describes alleged forged invoices, altered stock records and shortages of thousands of parts. The allegations are under investigation.

stories.headline: KPSC OPENS OBJECTION WINDOW FOR PROVISIONAL KAS RESULTS
paragraphs: The Karnataka Public Service Commission released provisional results for the 2026–27 KAS preliminary examination six days after the test. The recruitment covers 319 Gazetted Probationer posts.
Candidates disputing their provisional results can file supported objections online until 11 am on Monday. The commission says answer-key objections are not being accepted at this stage.

stories.headline: CUBBON PARK TO HOST 13-DAY FLOWER FESTIVAL FROM NOVEMBER 25
paragraphs: Cubbon Park will host its fifth flower show in 155 years, with the 13-day festival scheduled from November 25 to December 7. Organisers expect more than 15 lakh cut flowers and 1.2 lakh potted plants.
Planned displays include floral versions of Hoysala architecture, the Gandabherunda emblem and a Namma Metro coach, alongside exhibits and activities for families.

groups.ariaLabel: India climate, public policy and parliamentary news

stories.headline: COP31 COLLAPSES WITHOUT DEAL AFTER FOSSIL-FUEL ROW
paragraphs: Governments failed to reach an overarching agreement at COP31 in Antalya after the final proposal made no explicit mention of fossil fuels. The European Union and several countries said the text was too weak, while developing nations also objected to the climate-finance provisions.
The two-week talks ran nearly 48 hours past their scheduled close. The impasse is a setback for efforts to agree on a shared path for climate action.

stories.headline: RAJYA SABHA MP RAMRAO WADKUTE DIES AT 72
paragraphs: BJP Rajya Sabha member Ramrao Wadkute died in New Delhi after suffering a severe heart attack, party leaders said. He represented Maharashtra and had taken his oath as a member in April.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and other leaders expressed condolences, recalling Wadkute’s public service.

stories.headline: CJI CALLS FOR COMPULSORY LEGAL-AID WORK AND AI RULES IN LAW COURSES
paragraphs: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant proposed making a minimum period of legal-aid work a graduation requirement for law students. He also urged common guidelines for disclosing the use of AI in legal research.
The proposals were made at a legal-education conference in Hyderabad, where he argued for practical training and responsible use of new tools.

stories.headline: FSSAI SANCTIONS PROSECUTION AFTER BISLERI WATER SAMPLE FOUND UNSAFE
paragraphs: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after a packaged drinking-water sample was found unsafe and non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits.
The sample was sent for further testing after the company appealed; a laboratory again declared it unsafe. The regulator also sanctioned action against other firms and suspended two licences.

stories.headline: NINE PILGRIMS KILLED AS VEHICLE HITS PARKED TRUCK IN KOTA
paragraphs: Nine people from Maharashtra were killed and eight injured when their multi-utility vehicle struck a parked truck on the Kota–Udaipur highway while they were returning from a pilgrimage to Khatu Shyamji.
The injured were taken to hospital. Police are investigating the crash.

stories.headline: PM OPENS IIT PATNA AI CENTRE, ANNOUNCES RESEARCH PARK
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated an artificial-intelligence centre at IIT Patna and laid the foundation stone for a research park project.
The programme also included a proposed 120-bed startup hostel, part of a wider push to expand research and entrepreneurship infrastructure at the institute.

groups.ariaLabel: Indian cricket, chess and hockey news

stories.headline: TILAK VARMA CENTURY IN VAIN AS PAKISTAN A BEAT INDIA A
paragraphs: Tilak Varma scored a century and Abhishek Sharma made 70, but India A fell 48 runs short while chasing Pakistan A’s 314 in the Asia Cup Rising Stars match in Doha.
Pakistan set the target after posting 313. India lost early wickets, and the middle-order fightback could not complete the chase.

stories.headline: GUKESH AND SINDAROV SET FOR WORLD TITLE MATCH
paragraphs: World champion D Gukesh and challenger Javokhir Sindarov are preparing for Game 1 of the 2026 World Chess Championship on November 24 in Geneva. The match features the youngest title-match pairing in chess history.
Gukesh said he is approaching the contest with a winning mindset as the players begin the final stage of preparations.

stories.headline: INDIA FINISH UNBEATEN AND WIN CENTENARY HOCKEY SERIES
paragraphs: India drew 2–2 with New Zealand in the final match in Auckland to take the three-game Centenary of Sporting Unity series 1–0. India had won the opener 3–2 and drew the next two matches.
The series marked 100 years of sporting ties between the countries.
